This requirement gives a specific case (EX-2): if the repin step refuses a decision pinned to a reworded requirement, iaso opens a debug case and asks you nothing.

The change does the opposite. When a link is refused because its requirement was reworded, or because no model answered, iaso now opens no case. On a debug run, a case refused for a reworded requirement now counts as settled. The code comment says this follows two other requirements, SR-220 (EX-5) and SR-245 (#11). According to that comment, a reworded requirement is not a iaso bug: it waits or comes to you as a card.

Both can't be true at once. Either a reworded requirement is a iaso bug that iaso debugs quietly, or it's your call and comes to you as a card. Your intent only says "what it should handle", so it doesn't settle which. The turn that probably made this change has no prompt text, so it doesn't show what you asked for. Note: I took the link to SR-245 and SR-220 from the code comment and couldn't check that you've confirmed those two requirements.
